html:
Thaba Bosiu is a flat-topped sandstone mountain near Maseru, where Moshoeshoe I settled his people in 1824 and which became the capital and fortress of the Basotho kingdom.

Its steep cliffs and springs on the summit made it almost impossible to storm. Raiders, British troops and the Boers of the Orange Free State, who tried twice in the Free State wars of the 1860s, all failed to take it.

Moshoeshoe and later kings are buried on the summit. The mountain is the symbol of the nation's survival and a national monument of Lesotho, tied to the story of the Mfecane wars from which the kingdom was born.
